examples.knowledge_point: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given a Diagram
examples.problem:
In the diagram below, $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of $\mathbb{R}^2$, while $\mathbf{i'}$ and $\mathbf{j'}$ are their images under the linear transformation $\mathbf T.$
What is the standard matrix of $\mathbf T?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14060116/assets/4d1b9e56c0c6214d949d12f45fe4aecea5516971203724ecf573a2b17c6e959a.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in $\mathbb{R}^2$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf j$ under the action of the transformation.

feedback.problem: Given that ${i,j}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$ and that the images of $i$ and $j$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨-1,2⟩$ and $⟨3,-8⟩$, respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 2 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$
